label: Fortis Advisors v. Johnson & Johnson (Auris Health) — milestones, not a metric
provenance: PUBLIC RECORD, and the figures below are the ones two or more sources agree on. J&J/Ethicon's acquisition of Auris Health: up to $2.35 billion in contingent consideration tied to FDA regulatory milestones for the iPlatform and Monarch devices (Arnold & Porter advisory, Mar 2026), none of which was achieved after a change in the FDA's required clearance pathway. One named milestone is a $100 million 'Soft Tissue Ablation Milestone' (same source); an earlier summary describes it as a 510(k) clearance for lung tissue ablation. CAUTION: the litigation history is reported inconsistently across secondary sources — a post-trial Chancery award of more than $1 billion, a stipulated judgment of roughly $811 million in January 2026, and a Delaware Supreme Court decision of January 12, 2026 (No. 490,2024) that reversed the first-milestone ruling and vacated the related damages. This file does not rely on any of those figures; the only facts it uses are the milestone trigger and that no earnout was paid.
simplifications: Only the named $100 million milestone is expressed. The remaining milestones are not individually quantified in the sources used, and the total count is reported inconsistently, so no count is asserted here.

terms.eventDescription: FDA regulatory clearance, one of several milestones whose total count the sources report inconsistently

settled.note: No earnout was paid: the milestones were not achieved. The damages awarded in the litigation are not an earnout payment, were adjusted on appeal, and are not what this harness asserts.
